meta.title: CZ-6A Launch visibility
notes: Reconstruction (2026-11-28), not telemetry or a unique solution. Liftoff was reported at 13:05 UTC (21:05 Beijing time); the seconds are not known and 13:05:00 is used. It replaces the forecast of 2026-11-20, which re-timed the Yaogan-50 03 model to an assumed 13:01 liftoff.

This is the 732 km perigee profile of the corridor. Yaogan-50 02 and 04 were inserted at about 732 × 946 km (catalog mean elements), Yaogan-50 01 and 03 at about 702 × 945 km, all over the same booster zone: NOTAM A6107/26 has the same four vertices as the Yaogan-50 03 zone, and the catalog ground track passes 3.5 km beside the October model's.

Stage-2 cutoff is fixed at 13:18:45 UTC (T+825 s), an observation of this flight described as probable. The cutoff state is fitted to the first catalog elements of 2026-269A (assumed payload; identity unconfirmed) and lies 0.3 km and 0.13 m/s from that SGP4 state. Orbit data: Space-Track.org.

The vehicle is the same point-mass CZ-6A as for Yaogan-50 03 (published masses and thrusts, typical flight sequence, explicit drag). Its thrust direction follows one smooth law: vertical rise, pitch-over and gravity turn to T+90 s, then the tangent of the thrust elevation falls linearly in time to cutoff, continuous through staging (49° at T+90 s, 40° at stage separation, −7° at cutoff). Fitted thrust scale 0.987 against 1.06 from the December 2025 calibration; booster ballistic range 358 km against the 350 km zone; launch azimuth 255.5°.

The March 2026 triangulation of Yaogan-50 02, same orbit, lies within 3.9 km RMS of this path in altitude at the same longitude. Its times are not used. Stage 2 burns 585 s at an assumed 176.5 kN, from 38.9 t to 8.0 t; those masses scale with the assumed thrust. The two October ground reports carry little weight: their measurement error is unknown, and the model passes 1.69x the Moon's elevation where one report says 1.6x.

Sunlight pickup is the first moment the refracted Sun-centre ray clears the WGS84 ellipsoid: T+746.4 s, 13:17:26.4 UTC, at 724 km. The straight ray gives 13:17:46.8. The vehicle was observed leaving the Earth's shadow at 13:17:37 UTC, between the two, when the model gives 0.2% of full sunlight.

The first sunlight is weak and red: 1% of full Sun at 13:17:42, 10% at 13:17:51, 90% at 13:18:01, turning orange, cream, pale blue (ozone, about 13:17:49–58) and white. The observed plume was already blue at 13:17:37, 12 s before the modelled blue; the faint red seconds were not noticed. The page models none of that, nor weather, terrain, finite solar-disc emergence or plume size. Geometric visibility is not a claim of naked-eye detection.

The plane change starts in stage 1: the thrust stays in the launch plane until booster separation, so that the boosters fall into the zone of NOTAM A6107/26, then yaws out of it (4.4° by core cutoff) and continues smoothly through stage 2. How the turn is shared between the stages follows from that assumed law. Staging times follow the typical published CZ-6A sequence, not this flight's telemetry, and are not shown as timeline events.
NOTAM 12:53–13:15 UTC is a hazard-area activation interval, not launch-time limits or an insertion constraint. The 12:15–13:45 UTC selector is an exploratory range, not an announced launch window.
Shifting T0 reuses the same Earth-fixed (ECEF) trajectory and changes the solar geometry; it does not reoptimize dynamics or propagate a newly fitted orbit.

Source positions and velocities use a TEME-like frame with GMST rotation, UTC approximating UT1 and no polar motion. The exporter converts to ECEF and resamples with cubic Hermite interpolation; it does not reoptimize or integrate a new trajectory.
The upper-stage and orbit dynamics include central gravity and J2. Higher harmonics, post-insertion maneuvers, fragmentation and debris descent are not modeled.
Altitude samples are WGS84 geodetic ellipsoidal heights in km. Perigee and apogee are orbital radii minus the WGS84 equatorial radius; these are not the same altitude convention.

The 10° visibility envelope is sampled during sunlit ascent for sea-level observers with Sun-centre altitude ≤0°, then clipped to the observer night side at the insertion reference epoch. Post-insertion orbit tracks do not enlarge the ascent envelope.
The 1.5 revolutions shown are exactly 1.5 times the insertion Keplerian period in elapsed time, not a claim of an exact J2 ground-track repeat or true-anomaly recurrence.

The model TLE keeps the label PRELAUNCH MODEL - NOT OBSERVED and placeholder catalog number 00000. It is fitted to the reconstructed numerical orbit and is not the catalog element set; some TLE consumers reject this placeholder.

The rocket drawing follows that sequence: the four solid boosters burn to T+114.5 s and drop at T+117.5 s, the fairing at T+179 s and stage 1 at T+238.5 s; stage 2 ignites at T+240 s, and from insertion only the payload is drawn. These are drawing states, not timeline events.
about: Reconstruction from the observed cutoff time, the first catalog orbit and a calibrated CZ-6A vehicle model; not telemetry.
WGS84 geometry · JPL DE440s sunlight with refraction.

sunlight.model: Refracted Sun-centre ray clearing the WGS84 ellipsoid: US Standard Atmosphere 1976, refractivity 2.7758e-4 at sea level (550 nm), spherical Bouguer ray; no terrain, weather, extinction or solar-disc integration

source.status: CONDITIONAL RECONSTRUCTION — A CALIBRATED VEHICLE MODEL WITH ONE SMOOTH STEERING LAW, THE OBSERVED CUTOFF TIME AND THE FIRST CATALOG ORBIT; NOT TELEMETRY OR A UNIQUE SOLUTION
source.frame: TEME-like equator/equinox of date; GMST rotation with UTC used as UT1; not J2000
source.privacy: Only selected model parameters and basename/hash provenance are retained; no absolute source paths or raw Space-Track records are included.
